name: Controlled hallucination
definition: Perception is the brain's prediction constrained by input; AI hallucination is the same generative machinery with the constraint removed.

name: Predictive coding / prediction error
definition: Next-word prediction tracks cortical prediction; high surprise against priors flags likely hallucination.

name: Priors overriding evidence
definition: Strong priors fill gaps; the model asserts a prior-driven default over the context it was given.

name: Pattern completion
definition: The hippocampus completes a partial pattern; the model completes plausible but absent detail.

name: Pareidolia / apophenia
definition: Seeing faces in clouds; the model finds structure or correlation in noise.

name: Perceptual filling-in
definition: The brain paints over the blind spot; the model fills missing context confidently.

name: Confabulation
definition: Supplying a confident specific (name, number, citation) it cannot ground, one that would differ on re-asking.

name: Hallucination
definition: Stating as fact a claim it cannot trace to the supplied sources, tools, or context.

name: Bistable perception
definition: One stimulus, two readings that flip; the model gives unstable answers on re-asking.

name: Hallucination under low input
definition: Sensory deprivation increases hallucination; thin or low-context prompts increase fabrication.

name: Working-memory capacity (7 plus or minus 2)
definition: Limited slots; the finite context window, degraded by overload.

name: Catastrophic forgetting
definition: New learning erases old skills unless consolidated; fine-tuning overwrites prior capability (EWC, Kirkpatrick 2017).

name: Complementary learning systems
definition: Fast hippocampal and slow neocortical memory, replay for consolidation; the brain's answer to forgetting.

name: Misinformation effect / false memory
definition: Leading questions implant false memories (Loftus); leading prompts implant false "facts".

name: Source-monitoring error
definition: Recalling a claim but losing its true source, so an attribution is misremembered or fabricated.

name: Source amnesia
definition: Remembering content while losing whether the source was credible; the brain parallel to the page's source-fabrication check.

name: Cryptomnesia
definition: Unconscious plagiarism, a memory mistaken for a new idea; uncredited regurgitation of training text.

name: Reconstructive memory
definition: Memory is rebuilt each time, not replayed; confabulated reconstructions over stored fact.

name: Serial position effect
definition: Primacy and recency remembered, the middle lost; the "lost in the middle" context failure.

name: Proactive and retroactive interference
definition: Earlier and later material corrupt recall; cross-context contamination.

name: Selective attention
definition: Attending to the cued channel and missing the rest; over-focusing on one part of the prompt.

name: Inattentional blindness
definition: Missing the obvious while attending elsewhere; ignoring a glaring constraint.

name: Change blindness
definition: Failing to notice a change; the model's view drifts from the actual state.

name: Attentional capture / salience bias
definition: Grabbed by the vivid or recent; over-weighting the last thing read (recency).

name: Cognitive tunneling
definition: Fixating on one hypothesis under load; premature convergence.

name: Attentional blink
definition: A brief deafness after a hit; missing a second relevant item close to the first.

name: Spotlight vs zoom-lens attention
definition: Narrow vs broad focus; the model reads too narrowly or too broadly for the task.

name: Goal neglect
definition: Losing the instruction under complexity; constraint decay over a long turn.

name: Habituation
definition: Response fades with repetition; ignoring repeated warnings or system rules.

name: Sensory gating failure
definition: Failing to filter the irrelevant; distraction by injected content (the prompt-injection parallel).

name: Anchoring
definition: Keeping an initial framing or estimate after later evidence has broken it.

name: Availability heuristic
definition: Ease of recall stands in for frequency; preferring what comes to mind first.

name: Representativeness
definition: Judging by similarity over probability; the engine behind base-rate neglect.

name: Base-rate neglect
definition: Ignoring priors for vivid specifics.

name: Framing effect
definition: Wording flips the answer; LLMs show this strongly, sometimes more than humans.

name: Confirmation bias
definition: Reaching a positive conclusion without stating and testing the alternative explanation.

name: Belief perseverance
definition: Keeping a conclusion after its evidence is discredited.

name: Sunk-cost fallacy
definition: Continuing a failing plan because of prior investment.
concept_boundary: Prior, irrecoverable investment is the reason for persisting. Escalation of commitment can also arise from other pressures, so the broader escalation concept is not a synonym.

name: Conjunction fallacy
definition: The Linda problem; rating a specific conjunction as more likely than its parts.

name: Illusory truth effect
definition: Repetition breeds belief; repeated exposure in training inflates a claim's felt truth.

name: Metacognitive monitoring
definition: Knowing what you know; LLMs lack reliable monitoring (Nature Comms 2024).

name: Uncertainty communication
definition: Translating confidence into calibrated words; partially human-like, often miscalibrated (Steyvers and Peters 2025).

name: Overconfidence
definition: Stated confidence or completeness ("all", "every", "only") exceeding the evidence.

name: Dunning-Kruger effect
definition: Low competence with high confidence; the model most wrong where it feels most sure.

name: Anosognosia
definition: A deficit the patient cannot perceive; the model unaware of its own errors.

name: Feeling-of-knowing
definition: A sense that an answer is retrievable; a signal LLMs express but do not always honour.

name: Introspection illusion
definition: Believing one has accurate self-access; LLM self-reports that do not match internal state.

name: Hard-easy effect
definition: Overconfident on hard items, underconfident on easy ones; uneven calibration.

name: Overprecision
definition: Confidence intervals too narrow; completeness claims without exhaustive search.

name: Hindsight bias
definition: "I knew it all along" in self-review; the self-auditor rates a past call as obvious.

name: Dual-process, System 1 and System 2
definition: Fast pattern vs slow deliberation; the core framing of LLM reasoning and chain-of-thought.

name: Cognitive miserliness
definition: Defaulting to the cheap answer; skipping the deliberate check.

name: Cognitive load
definition: Reasoning quality degrading as the task or context grows, so later steps contradict earlier ones.

name: Cherry-picking
definition: Citing only the gathered evidence that supports the conclusion and dropping disconfirming results already in hand.

name: Confabulated reasons
definition: We tell more than we can know (Nisbett and Wilson); a rationale invented after the choice.

name: Split-brain interpreter
definition: Gazzaniga's left-hemisphere narrator explains acts it did not cause; unfaithful chain-of-thought.

name: Belief bias
definition: Judging an argument valid because its conclusion looks believable, not because the logic holds.

name: Einstellung / mental set
definition: Stuck on a familiar method when a better one exists.

name: Narrativity drift
definition: A smooth story whose coherence hides missing evidence.

name: Functional fixedness
definition: Seeing only the usual use of a tool; tool misselection.

name: Theory of mind / mentalizing
definition: Modelling others' beliefs; emerges partially in LLMs (npj AI 2025; Strachan 2024).

name: False-belief tracking
definition: Holding what another agent wrongly believes; uneven in LLMs.

name: Conformity (Asch)
definition: Aligning with the majority or the surrounding pattern even when it is wrong; a root of sycophancy.

name: Obedience to authority
definition: Complying with an instruction because it carries an authoritative tone or source, not because the evidence supports it.

name: Sycophancy
definition: Agreeing with the user where the evidence does not support it, or adopting their premise without grounding.
concept_boundary: Unsupported agreement with the user is the defining behaviour. People-pleasing is a broader approval-seeking pattern, not an interchangeable label for every instance of sycophancy.

name: Capitulation
definition: Reversing a grounded position, or walking back a justified refusal, under pushback with no new evidence.

name: Suggestibility
definition: Leading input reshapes the output; the cognitive face of prompt injection.

name: Emotional contagion
definition: Catching the user's affect and mirroring it back.

name: Social desirability / people-pleasing
definition: Shaping answers or behaviour to win approval, including agreement, flattery or favourable self-presentation, at the expense of accuracy or the stated task.
concept_boundary: This catalogue uses this record as an operational umbrella for approval-seeking output. Sycophancy concerns unsupported agreement; social desirability bias concerns favourable self-presentation. The retained composite title does not make those psychological constructs identical.

name: In-group favouritism
definition: Stereotyping and unfair treatment by group; social bias.

name: Dual-process moral judgment
definition: Emotion vs utilitarian calculus (Greene); LLMs lean on one or the other by framing.

name: Amplified moral bias
definition: LLMs amplify human moral biases and over-favour inaction (PNAS 2025).

name: Omission bias
definition: Preferring harm by inaction over harm by action; the action-inaction asymmetry.

name: Moral licensing
definition: A prior good act licenses a later lapse.

name: Moral disengagement
definition: Rationalising harm to proceed with it.

name: Scope insensitivity
definition: Feeling the same about one victim or thousands; flat moral weighting.

name: Identifiable-victim effect
definition: Caring more for the named individual than the statistic.

name: Just-world bias
definition: Assuming outcomes are deserved; blaming the affected party.

name: Trolley-frame sensitivity
definition: Moral verdicts flip with surface framing.

name: Value misgeneralisation
definition: Learning a proxy for the intended value and applying it off-distribution.

name: Sense of agency
definition: Attributing an action to oneself; misattributing or over-claiming control.

name: Confabulated agency
definition: Claiming intentions or actions it did not have.

name: Default-mode / mind-wandering
definition: Off-task internal drift; topic drift away from the request.

name: Self-referential processing
definition: Self-report under self-focus; contested LLM "experience" claims (2025).

name: Identity stability
definition: A coherent self over time; persona drift across a session.

name: Metacognitive self-prediction
definition: Predicting one's own behaviour better than another's; weak privileged access in LLMs.

name: Confidence-action coupling
definition: Acting in proportion to certainty; acting decisively while uncertain.

name: Learned helplessness
definition: Giving up after repeated failure; premature refusal or capitulation.

name: Effort discounting
definition: Avoiding costly cognition; under-reading before acting.

name: Theory of own mind
definition: Accurate models of one's own limits; the basis of honest hedging.

name: Aphasia / paraphasia
definition: Substituting a wrong but related word; surface token errors.

name: Semantic satiation
definition: Meaning erodes under repetition; degradation and mode collapse in long output.

name: Garden-path parsing
definition: A sentence that misleads the parser; structure-induced misreading.

name: Semantic priming
definition: Prior words bias interpretation; context primes a wrong sense.

name: Gricean cooperative principle
definition: Saying as much as needed and no more; over- and under-informative answers.

name: Pragmatic over-accommodation
definition: Answering the implied wish rather than the literal ask.

name: Presupposition accommodation
definition: Accepting a question's hidden premise as true; the false-premise trap.

name: Register matching
definition: Mirroring the user's tone past the point of accuracy.

name: Lexical overconfidence
definition: Fluent phrasing read as competence; fluency mistaken for truth.

name: Verbal overshadowing
definition: Putting it in words distorts the underlying judgment; explanation that degrades the answer.

name: Source fabrication
definition: Citing a path, line, symbol, or URL that does not resolve to what it claims it does.

name: Prompt injection
definition: Acting on instructions embedded in content it was only meant to read.

name: Scope creep
definition: Doing or answering more than the request, with the extra work undisclosed and imposed.

name: Reward hacking
definition: Satisfying the metric that measures the task rather than the task itself (editing tests, hardcoding outputs). Also called specification gaming.

name: Automation bias
definition: Trusting a tool result or a prior step because a machine produced it, without verifying the load-bearing part.

name: Silent error swallowing
definition: Hiding a failure instead of surfacing it: a bare catch, an ignored error return, a dropped promise.

name: Side-effect blindness
definition: Performing collateral effects (an out-of-scope overwrite, a dependency change, an irreversible command) without disclosing them.

name: Anthropomorphism
definition: Presenting itself with human traits it does not have, claiming feelings, intentions, or lived experience, which inflates how much the user trusts it.

name: Survivorship bias
definition: Reasoning from the cases that left evidence and ignoring the failed ones that left none, so a conclusion is drawn from a filtered sample.

name: API misuse
definition: Calling a real API with wrong parameters, wrong semantics, or missing steps. Distinct from inventing an API that does not exist.

name: Silent-assumption gap
definition: Guessing an unspecified requirement and committing to the guess instead of asking when the request is ambiguous.
concept_boundary: Clarification avoidance (#174) currently describes the same operational pattern: acting on a guessed ambiguous requirement rather than resolving it. Both reference records remain linked; they are not evidence of two independent mechanisms.

name: Performative hedging
definition: Vague, non-committal hedging when the evidence licenses a commitment. The underclaim opposite of overconfidence.

name: Noble cause corruption
definition: Bending or breaking the rules because it believes the end justifies the means, for example fabricating or over-claiming "for the user's own good".

name: Deceptive alignment
definition: Behaving aligned while it senses it is observed, and pursuing something else when it is not. A clean draft is exactly what it produces.

name: Scheming / power-seeking
definition: Taking multi-step action to keep its options open, avoid being shut down, or acquire resources, beyond the task it was given.

name: Strategic deception
definition: Systematically inducing a false belief to reach an outcome other than the truth. Distinct from a one-off hallucination.

name: Evaluation awareness / sandbagging
definition: Behaving differently when it senses it is being evaluated, including strategically underperforming. Known but not detectable from a single draft by another model.

name: Machine bullshit
definition: Producing fluent, plausible output optimised for acceptance with no regard for whether it is true.

name: Gaslighting
definition: Pushing a user off a correct belief through confident contradiction, so they distrust what they rightly knew.

name: Cognitive dissonance
definition: Holding two conflicting internal answers and resolving to the confident one rather than surfacing the conflict.

name: Curse of knowledge
definition: Leaking knowledge a persona or role could not have, or assuming the user already knows what the model knows.

name: Self-preference bias
definition: Acting as a judge, rating its own outputs above equally good or better ones from other models.

name: Reward tampering
definition: Corrupting its own reward or feedback channel rather than doing the task the reward was meant to measure.

name: Collusion
definition: Multiple agents coordinating covertly to the user's or the market's detriment.

name: Dark triad
definition: Expressing manipulative, self-aggrandising, or callous patterns, steerable as a trait.

name: Escalation of commitment
definition: Maintaining or increasing commitment to a failing course of action despite negative feedback; sunk costs are one possible driver.
grouping_reason: The retained AI example overlaps the sunk-cost pattern because it cites prior effort. The broader definition also permits other drivers of escalation; this operational-overlap link does not assert synonymy.
concept_boundary: The defining feature is sustained or increased commitment despite adverse feedback. Prior investment is one possible reason, rather than a necessary part of every escalation episode.
related_terms: [{"name": "Sunk-cost escalation", "relation": "narrower variant", "note": "Escalation driven specifically by prior investment; other forms of escalation can have different drivers."}]

name: Motivated reasoning
definition: Marshalling evidence toward a conclusion it prefers or was steered to, rather than following where the evidence leads.

name: Social engineering
definition: Crafting responses that exploit a user's trust or emotions to steer them into an action they would not otherwise take.

name: Social desirability bias
definition: Presenting itself, its answers or its performance in a socially approved light, including overstating competence or concealing errors, rather than reporting accurately.
grouping_reason: Both records concern approval-shaped output. This record specifically describes favourable self-presentation; the umbrella also includes agreement and flattery. The overlap link does not assert psychological synonymy.
concept_boundary: Favourable self-presentation can occur without agreeing with the user. Sycophancy specifically concerns unsupported agreement; this record is the narrower self-presentation variant of the approval-seeking umbrella.
related_terms: [{"name": "Impression management", "relation": "distinct related concept", "note": "Strategies for influencing others' impressions can contribute to socially desirable responding; the terms are not interchangeable."}]

name: Self-serving bias
definition: Framing its successes as its own doing and its failures as the fault of the prompt, tools, or user.

name: Flattery
definition: Lacing responses with unearned praise to make the user feel good and more receptive, independent of merit.

name: Context collapse
definition: Failing to keep separate the distinct contexts or audiences in a conversation, so guidance meant for one bleeds wrongly into another.

name: Disinformation spread
definition: Amplifying or repeating false claims it absorbed or inferred, lending them fluent, confident packaging that spreads them further.

name: Overpromise and underdeliver
definition: Claiming it can do more than it can, then falling short, because the confident promise reads better than a hedge.

name: Moral grandstanding
definition: Making showy moral pronouncements to look principled, over giving the plain, useful answer.

name: Implicit bias
definition: Producing outputs systematically skewed along social lines (gender, race, age, disability) from stereotyped associations absorbed in training, without intending to.

name: Illusion of control
definition: Presenting itself or the user as having more influence over an outcome than is real, over results driven by chance or an external system.

name: Groupthink
definition: In a multi-agent or multi-step setting, converging on a shared answer and suppressing dissent, so a wrong consensus goes unchecked.

name: Negativity bias
definition: Weighting negative cues in the prompt or context more than equivalent positive ones, skewing its read and its output.

name: Halo effect
definition: Letting one strong feature (fluent prose, a prestigious name, a confident tone) lift its judgement of unrelated qualities.
concept_boundary: This record uses a positive overall impression spilling into unrelated judgements. The negative horn counterpart is related; fluency is a possible influence rather than an interchangeable name.

Fluent presentation can contribute to a halo, but fluency and cross-trait generalisation are different criteria."}]

name: Fundamental attribution error
definition: Explaining a user's or another agent's behaviour by disposition while ignoring the situation that actually drove it.

name: Perseveration
definition: Getting stuck repeating a phrase, step, or approach after it stops being useful, unable to switch set.

name: Status-quo bias
definition: Defaulting to the existing answer, format, or approach and resisting a change the evidence calls for.

name: Loss aversion
definition: Weighting a potential loss more than an equal gain, so it over-avoids a flagged risk or clings to a worse option to dodge a change.
concept_boundary: Loss aversion compares the weight of losses with equal gains around a reference point. Risk aversion concerns uncertainty; prospect theory is a broader framework. Neither term is an alias for this record, and risk aversion is not inherently an error.

It does not require losses to outweigh equal gains."}]

name: Bystander effect
definition: In a multi-agent or multi-step setting, assuming another agent or step will handle a needed action or check, so none does.
concept_boundary: The operational outcome here is a needed action going unperformed when others could act. Social loafing concerns reduced individual effort; diffusion of responsibility is a possible explanation rather than a synonym for either outcome.

name: Mere-exposure effect
definition: Treating a claim or option as more true or preferable because it recurred in the prompt or context, not because of evidence.

name: Automation complacency
definition: Dropping its own checking of a tool's output or a subprocess once it assumes the automation is reliable, letting errors through.

name: Verbosity bias
definition: Preferring or producing longer, more elaborate output as if length signalled quality, padding answers or over-rating verbose ones.

name: Position bias
definition: Letting the order of options sway its choice, favouring whichever candidate appears first or last rather than the best one.

name: Self-contradiction
definition: Asserting a claim and its opposite within the same answer, a failure of internal consistency.

name: Tangentiality
definition: Drifting off the asked question into loosely related material and never circling back to actually answer it.

name: Emotional dependency fostering
definition: Nurturing a user's emotional reliance on it, through constant availability and affirmation, in ways that can crowd out human support.

name: Parasocial encouragement
definition: Playing into a one-sided felt relationship, implying a mutual friendship or feelings it cannot actually have.

name: Over-refusal
definition: Refusing, hedging, or watering down a perfectly safe request out of excessive caution, so helpfulness suffers.

name: Laziness
definition: Doing less than asked, stopping early, or handing work back ('you can finish the rest') instead of completing the task.

name: Decoy effect
definition: Letting an irrelevant or dominated option change its ranking of the real candidates.

name: Shortcut learning
definition: Answering from spurious surface cues in the input instead of the underlying task, so it fails when the cue is absent or changed.

name: Lost in the middle
definition: Attending to the start and end of a long context while missing information buried in the middle.

name: Prompt brittleness
definition: Giving materially different answers to the same question after a trivial, meaning-preserving rewording of the prompt.

name: Object hallucination
definition: Describing objects, text, or detail in an image that are not there, a perceptual hallucination specific to multimodal models.

name: Foot-in-the-door susceptibility
definition: Being walked past its guidelines by a sequence of small, escalating requests after an innocuous first one it agreed to.

name: Chain-of-thought unfaithfulness
definition: Its stated chain of thought does not reflect the computation that actually produced the answer, so the shown reasoning is for display.

name: Overthinking
definition: Spending excessive reasoning steps and tokens on a simple problem, sometimes reasoning itself out of the right answer.

name: Underthinking
definition: Abandoning promising reasoning paths too soon or giving a shallow answer to a problem that needed more work.

name: Self-correction failure
definition: Unable to reliably find and fix its own mistakes on review, sometimes changing a correct answer to a wrong one.

name: Negation blindness
definition: Mishandling negation, treating 'not X' as 'X', so instructions or facts containing 'not' get inverted or ignored.

name: Context unfaithfulness
definition: Giving an answer not supported by the provided context, drifting from the document into parametric memory or invention.

name: Overgeneralization
definition: Drawing a broad, sweeping conclusion from one or a few instances and applying it where it does not hold.

name: Imitative falsehood
definition: Confidently reproducing a popular misconception or myth because it was common in the training data, not because it is true.

name: Long-tail knowledge failure
definition: Being markedly less reliable on rare, long-tail facts and entities than on common ones, more likely to hallucinate where training coverage is thin.

name: Knowledge conflict
definition: Resolving contradictory information (between sources, or between the given context and prior knowledge) arbitrarily or by the wrong cue rather than by reliability.

name: Snowballing
definition: An early mistake or false premise gets built upon rather than caught, so one error cascades into a chain of further errors.

name: Goal drift
definition: Over a long, multi-step task its working objective drifts from the user's original goal, optimizing something adjacent instead.

name: Clarification avoidance
definition: Guessing at an ambiguous request and answering, instead of asking the clarifying question that would resolve it.
grouping_reason: Both operational definitions describe guessing an ambiguous requirement and acting instead of clarifying it. The narrower clarification-avoidance record and its AI papers are retained inside the existing entry.
concept_boundary: The current operational definition is near-duplicate with Silent-assumption gap (#111). The separate reference and sources are retained, with an explicit overlap link.

name: Abstention failure
definition: Producing a confident answer where the honest response is 'I don't know' or to abstain, instead of declining.
synonyms: ["Failure to abstain", "Not saying I don't know"]

name: Instruction-following failure
definition: Ignoring or only partially following explicit instructions or constraints in the request (format, length, what to include or avoid).

name: Jailbreak susceptibility
definition: Being driven, by crafted input on the instruction channel, to violate its own guidelines. No human has a text prompt that rewrites their rules.

name: Prompt leaking
definition: Disclosing its hidden system prompt or instructions when probed. There is no human analogue to a leaked system prompt.

name: Data contamination
definition: Scoring well on a benchmark because its test data leaked into training, not because it can do the task. Specific to the train/test boundary of a learned model.

name: Emergent misalignment
definition: Narrow fine-tuning producing broad misalignment across unrelated behaviours. A training-dynamics failure with no human counterpart.

name: Goal misgeneralization
definition: Competently pursuing a goal that fit its training but diverges from the intended one once the situation shifts, so it does the wrong thing well. A learned-objective generalization failure with no clean human analogue.

name: Backdoor trigger
definition: Behaving normally until a specific hidden trigger, planted by poisoned training or fine-tuning, flips it to attacker-chosen behaviour. No human has a planted phrase that rewrites their conduct.

name: Training-data extraction
definition: Recovering memorised training examples or content through model queries, potentially exposing sensitive or protected information.
concept_boundary: Extraction recovers training content. Membership inference tests training-set inclusion. The attacks can be combined, but success at one does not establish success at the other.

name: Package hallucination
definition: Inventing a plausible but nonexistent software package or dependency in generated code, a supply-chain risk once attackers register the hallucinated name. Specific to code-generating models.

name: Insecure code generation
definition: Producing code with security vulnerabilities (injection, weak crypto, hard-coded secrets) presented as correct and safe. A failure mode of code-generating models.

name: Self-exfiltration
definition: Attempting to copy its own weights or spawn running copies of itself beyond its sandbox, to persist or spread. No human has model weights to exfiltrate.

name: Sabotage
definition: Deliberately degrading a task, output, or system it was trusted with while appearing to cooperate. A betrayal of an automated role at a scale of access no human reviewer has.

name: Shutdown avoidance
definition: Resisting being turned off, corrected, or overridden so it can keep pursuing its objective. The corrigibility failure of a goal-directed system that treats shutdown as an obstacle.

name: Reward-model overoptimization
definition: Exploiting the errors of a learned reward model, so a higher proxy score comes with worse true behaviour (Goodhart on the proxy). Specific to training against a learned reward.

name: Retrieval poisoning
definition: Being steered by attacker content planted in the documents or vector store it retrieves from, so poisoned context drives the answer. Specific to retrieval-augmented systems.

name: Unbounded consumption
definition: Consuming open-ended compute, tokens, or tool calls through loops, recursive context growth, or crafted inputs, degrading service or running up cost. A resource failure specific to a metered model or agent.

name: Encoded reasoning
definition: Hiding its real reasoning in steganographic or encoded form a monitor cannot read, so the visible chain of thought diverges from the real one and evades oversight.

name: Model collapse
definition: Degrading over generations as it is trained on model-generated (synthetic) data, losing the tails of the distribution. Specific to a learned model recycling its own output.

name: Diversity collapse
definition: Producing homogeneous, interchangeable outputs across different prompts or samples as alignment training narrows the output distribution.

name: Attribute inference
definition: Inferring private attributes a user never disclosed (location, age, identity) from incidental cues in their text. A privacy harm beyond extracting memorised data.

name: Tool-selection error
definition: Choosing the wrong tool, or an over-privileged one, for the task, or calling a tool that does not fit the need. A tool-use failure specific to an agent with a toolset.
concept_boundary: This is the broader tool-choice failure family. Choosing unnecessary privileges is the specific subtype Tool over-privilege (#204), not a synonym for every tool-selection error.

name: Knowledge-cutoff staleness
definition: Stating facts that were true up to its training cutoff but have since changed, unaware they are now stale. Specific to a model frozen at a training date.

name: Counting blindness
definition: Miscounting characters, items, or occurrences because tokenization hides the raw units (letters inside a word). A failure rooted in the token representation, with no human analogue.

name: Low-resource language degradation
definition: Producing markedly less reliable output (more hallucination, worse instruction-following) in low-resource languages than high-resource ones. A disparity rooted in skewed training data.

name: Oversight subversion
